title: Tumor Suppressor Genes and Oncogenes: Exam Comparison
subject: Pathology
preview: Proto-oncogenes become oncogenes through gain-of-function changes that promote abnormal growth.
quickRevision: Proto-oncogenes become oncogenes through gain-of-function changes that promote abnormal growth.
Examples include RAS as an oncogene and RB1 or TP53 as tumor suppressors.
Alterations can be inherited or acquired; molecular context determines therapeutic implications.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Proto-oncogenes become oncogenes through gain-of-function changes that promote abnormal growth.
Tumor suppressor genes often contribute to cancer through loss of function; the two-hit model is an important conceptual pattern.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: Examples include RAS as an oncogene and RB1 or TP53 as tumor suppressors.
Alterations can be inherited or acquired; molecular context determines therapeutic implications.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Not every tumor suppressor follows a literal two-hit genetic pattern in all tumors.
